narrative.overview:
The systems evidence ledger treats the portfolio as an authored record of business problems, technical contribution, and supported outcomes. It borrows the discipline of requirements traceability, operational change records, and engineering case files without imitating a dashboard.

The interface is precise, quiet, and human. Cool mineral surfaces, carbon text, cobalt annotations, numbered folios, and hairline rules establish a continuous reading system; asymmetrical evidence layouts and authentic artifacts keep the work itself in command.
keyCharacteristics: Flat mineral surfaces divided by precise rules.
One cobalt annotation color across actions and evidence markers.
Onest narrative type paired with sparse monospace metadata.
Desktop folio rails that collapse into the mobile reading flow.
Authentic portraits and repository artifacts presented as documented exhibits.

rules.name: The Cobalt Annotation Rule
rules.body: Cobalt marks actions, folios, links, and small evidence signals; it never becomes a broad decorative field.

rules.name: The Theme Pair Rule
rules.body: Light and dark modes swap complete role sets; never mix a light surface token with dark-mode copy or rule tokens.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Onest carries narrative and hierarchy; monospace is reserved for evidence metadata, not personality or decoration.

rules.name: The Rail-to-Flow Rule
rules.body: The folio rail appears only when the viewport can sustain it; below 64rem it becomes an inline section header without changing reading order.

rules.name: The Ruled Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Use border lines and deliberate vertical intervals to group evidence; do not wrap every unit in a container.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Major content surfaces stay flat at rest; shadow is reserved for a temporary layer that physically overlaps the document.

rules.name: The Almost-Square Rule
rules.body: Two-pixel action corners are the maximum recurring radius; larger rounding, capsules, and decorative pills do not belong in the ledger.

dos: Do use evidence labels, folios, captions, and rules to make contribution and context easy to trace.
Do keep Cobalt Signal rare enough that every appearance reads as action or annotation.
Do present repository screenshots and portraits as flat exhibits with honest captions.
Do vary evidence-layout proportions while preserving a clear semantic reading order.
Do preserve 2.75rem minimum interaction targets, visible focus, dark-mode role parity, and reduced-motion behavior.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glow, glass effects, or decorative saturation.
Don't turn evidence into repeated rounded cards, bento tiles, chips, or skill-logo walls.
Don't imitate a dashboard, add fake case-study artifacts, or imply unsupported authorship.
Don't use large radii, decorative pills, or shadows on persistent content surfaces.
Don't give every project, role, or capability equal visual emphasis.
